text:
Maya: quick heads-up — repro'd a ~12% median latency regression when the scheduler picked flashx-lite for fused+paged attention on long seq (2048). baseline was flashv3. perf-bot run attached below.

PerfBot: summary: run=2026-03-17T18:10Z model=gpt-6b seq=2048 concurrency=16 microbatch=1 kernel=flashx-lite
  median_latency=142.3ms (prev 127.6ms)
  p95=210.9ms (prev 183.1ms)
  avg_gpu_bw=840GB/s (device peak 900GB/s)
  smem_util_avg=78%
  sm_lane_stalls=24%

Arjun: what was the kernel selector decision path? did we fall back to a paged variant or choose a fusion with smaller tile?

Maya: selector log: 
  - request: seq=2048, kv_cache=true, route=fused+paged
  - candidate kernels: [flashv3-fuse, flashx-lite, flash-paged-merge]
  - scoring: cost_model favored flashx-lite (lower estimated DRAM pressure)
  - chosen: flashx-lite

Maya: repro command: 
  ```bash
  ./bench_runner --model gpt-6b --seq 2048 --concurrency 16 --kv-cache on --batching micro=1 --kernel-override flashx-lite
  ```

Lucy: screenshots from nsight show a hotter SM shared memory path under flashx-lite — more bank conflicts around the tail of attention. lowering pipeline stages from 3->2 moved some pressure to registers and reduced sm_lane_stalls to ~16%.

Pete: also seeing KV cache eviction jitter. when many concurrent requests hit slightly different prefix lengths we get small cascades of KV writes that inflate DRAM traffic. that could push avg_gpu_bw up and make flashx-lite's higher SM usage worse.

Sasha: can we try two quick axes: (1) force flashv3 on fused+paged to verify regression is kernel-specific, (2) run flashx-lite with occupancy tweak (max_warps=20 -> 18) and pipeline=2?

Maya: started runs: 
  - run A (force flashv3): ./bench_runner --kernel-override flashv3-fuse -> median 128.9ms (close to baseline)
  - run B (flashx-lite pipeline=2 occupancy=18): median 133.1ms (improved but still ~4% reg vs baseline)

PerfBot: additional metrics (run B):
  avg_gpu_bw=805GB/s
  smem_util_avg=67%
  sm_lane_stalls=15%
  l2_read_bandwidth=420GB/s

Arjun: interesting — forcing flashv3 confirms regression is introduced by flashx-lite path. but pipeline/occupancy tuning helps. implies kernel's tiling or register/refill strategy is suboptimal for our KV access pattern.

Lucy: hypotheses: 
  - flashx-lite's tile size increases shared memory reuse but causes strided bank conflicts when KV cache line offsets are non-uniform.
  - microbatching heuristic (micro=1) leaves little time for KV prefetching; combined with flashx-lite's inner loop it amplifies stalls.

Pete: short experiment: add a small jittered prefix-aligner to KV lookups (pad to 128B boundaries) — reduces bank conflict variance. it's messy but cheap to test.

Sasha: also try changing max_batch_size from 32 -> 8 to force smaller bursts and see if scheduler-induced BW storms go away.

Maya: logging a quick flame snippet for run A vs run B (ascii):
  run A (flashv3): [compute: 65%][l2: 20%][mem-copy: 15%]
  run B (flashx-lite pipeline=2): [compute: 58%][l2: 30%][mem-copy: 12%]
  note: l2 jumps in flashx-lite case which matches higher DRAM prefetch churn.

Arjun: action items: 
  1) perf/engine team to add a selector feature flag to bias against flashx-lite on seq>=1024 + kv_cache=true for 2 days while we root-cause (Maya).
  2) runtime to experiment with pipeline stages and occupancy knobs to produce a perf matrix (Lucy + Sasha).
  3) infra to add lightweight KV prefix padding probe on a small % of traffic to measure bank-conflict impact (Pete).
  4) if we confirm kernel bug, coordinate with kernel owner to adjust tile/stride (Arjun).

Maya: I'll push the selector flag and roll it out to canary 5% now and monitor latency SLO. @PerfBot please kick daily summary for this thread. :eyes:

PerfBot: acknowledged — will post daily deltas and attach scheduler/kernel decision logs.

Lucy: one final note — also check quantized kernels (int8-fused) — they change register pressure and sometimes side-step SM conflicts entirely. worth a quick A/B.

Maya: thanks team. I'll update the thread with canary metrics and raw nsight captures. :thumbsup:
